### workspace cleanup --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace cleanup [options]

Detect and remove zombie sessions from state.
A zombie session is one where the state file has an entry but
the corresponding tmux session or iTerm window no longer exists.

Lists all zombie sessions and asks for confirmation before removing.

Options:
    -f, --force                      Skip confirmation and remove zombies immediately
        --dry-run                    List what would be removed; no prompt, nothing changes, exit 0
        --tmux-dead-only             Count only entries whose tmux session is gone (a closed window alone
                                     does not make an entry a zombie)
        --json                       Print one action document (see docs/README.json.md) instead of text, which goes
                                     to stderr; without --force the prompt still asks (or fails under --no-input).
                                     Rows carry tmux_alive and window_alive (null: headless, or iTerm's windows
                                     could not be listed; a window that could not be read is never called gone)

Examples:
  workspace cleanup    # list zombie sessions and ask before removing them from state
  workspace cleanup --dry-run --json    # report the zombies, change nothing
  workspace cleanup --tmux-dead-only --force    # remove only entries with no tmux session
  workspace cleanup --force    # remove all zombie sessions immediately
--- stderr
--- end
